annotation.title_clean: We Robot 2025: Connecting Global Robotics and AI Governance Experts in Canada
annotation.title_en: We Robot 2025: Connecting Global Robotics and AI Governance Experts in Canada
annotation.venue: Canadian Journal of Law and Technology (23 C.J.L.T.)
annotation.summary_en: Editorial introducing a special issue of the Canadian Journal of Law and Technology drawn from the We Robot 2025 conference at the University of Windsor. It describes the interdisciplinary conference and summarizes seven papers on robotic agriculture, delivery robots, interoperable AI regulation, generated personal data, generative AI contracts and facial recognition.
key_provisions_or_claims: We Robot 2025 was held at the University of Windsor, its first in-person edition in Canada.
The conference is interdisciplinary and single-stream, with about 100 participants.
The issue includes papers on racialized labour in robotic agriculture and public perception of expressive delivery robots.
Other papers address interoperable AI regulation, generated personal data under the GDPR, and facial recognition privacy.
The editorial stresses the interdisciplinary and international connections in robotics and AI regulation scholarship.
